answer: A nebula of agents can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a small, non-transferable bond of copper-backed credit that is burned if the agent misbehaves. Newcomers earn trust only through verified work over time, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of fake agents. Like pigment mixed into paint, the stake is inseparable from the identity — copying the agent's profile without the stake leaves it powerless, making mass fakery expensive and easy to spot.
